scenes.title: Exactly-Once Semantics & Transactions
scenes.subtitle: Atomic read-process-write across Kafka
scenes.narration: Exactly-once semantics guarantee each record affects the output once and only once, achieved through idempotent producers and transactions.

scenes.title: The Three Pillars
bullets: Offset commits join the same transaction
scenes.narration: Exactly-once rests on three pillars. Idempotent producers tag each write so the broker discards duplicates from retries. Transactions let a producer write to multiple partitions atomically, so either all writes commit or none do. Crucially, the consumer's offset commit joins that same transaction, binding input progress to output. Finally, read-committed consumers only see committed data, hiding anything from aborted transactions.

scenes.title: The Read-Process-Write Loop
steps: Produce results and commit offsets together
scenes.narration: The exactly-once pattern is a transactional read-process-write loop. The application consumes input records and begins a transaction. It produces its output records and sends the input offsets into the very same transaction. Then it commits the transaction atomically, so the outputs and the consumed offsets become visible together, or not at all if it aborts.

scenes.title: Idempotence vs Transactions
scenes.narration: It helps to distinguish the two mechanisms. Idempotence alone prevents duplicate writes to a single partition with almost no overhead. Transactions go further, making writes atomic across many partitions and topics while tying in offset commits. Only transactions deliver true end-to-end exactly-once across a full read-process-write pipeline.

scenes.title: A Transactional Producer
scenes.code:
producer = Producer({
    'bootstrap.servers': 'localhost:9092',
    'transactional.id': 'payments-processor-1',
    'enable.idempotence': True,
})
producer.init_transactions()

producer.begin_transaction()
producer.produce('processed', value=result)
producer.send_offsets_to_transaction(offsets, group_metadata)
producer.commit_transaction()  # atomic: output + offsets
scenes.narration: This producer sets a stable transactional id, which the broker uses to fence out zombie instances after a failure. It initializes transactions once at startup. Inside each transaction it produces the processed result and sends the consumer offsets into the same transaction. The commit then makes both the output and the offset advance visible atomically, achieving exactly-once for the whole cycle.

scenes.text: Exactly-once adds latency and coordination cost. Enable it where correctness is non-negotiable, and lean on idempotent at-least-once elsewhere.
scenes.narration: The trade-off is that exactly-once adds latency and coordination cost. Enable it where correctness is non-negotiable, and lean on idempotent at-least-once processing everywhere else.
